newsitem.title: USA: Schroder & Co snares exodus of NatWest employees.
newsitem.headline: Schroder & Co snares exodus of NatWest employees.

text.p: Several top executives of National Westminster Bank Plc unit NatWest Markets have left the investment bank to head up a health care corporate finance and research team at Schroder & Co Inc.

Schroder said Wednesday it hired former Natwest managing directors Bradley Razook, who headed health care corporate finance at NatWest, and Peter Sidoti, who ran research in health care and real estate, with several of their coworkers.
Razook will head the corporate finance health care group and Sidoti will join the research department, Schroder said.

Also joining from NatWest are managing directors Laurent de Marval and Bradford Wildauer, in health care corporate finance, as well as Jeffrey Bagley and Ray Lewis, who will join in the research department.

"This addition .... will immediately create an integrated research/corporate finance group in health care," said Schroder executives Gerry Grimstone and Barry Tarasoff in a statement. "Since 1991, Mr. Razook, Mr. Sidoti and their team were instrumental in over $8 billion of equity and equity-linked financings in addition to conducting a sizable M&A business," they said.

About two dozen people specializing in healthcare and technology joined the exodus from NatWest to Schroder & Co, including analysts and bankers, according to market sources. Schroder would not comment on the exact number of people joining the firm. NatWest Markets would not comment on the departures at all.

Schroder said it would also add a "Micro-Cap Research Group," adding 150 companies to its research universe. The group should be able to snare "numerous attractive underwriting opportunities," it said.
Just last week, an industry trade publication said Merrill Lynch and Co Inc in London landed three NatWest telecommunications professionals.
